newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols off highs as spot pauses.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols off highs as spot pauses.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options came off from early highs in U.S. trading as the dollar's almost daily intrusion into multi-year-high territory took a pause, dealers said.
Ted Voorhees, a senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York, said the 1.84-mark level was proving to be tough resistance to break through.
"As a result, the market's disappointed and volatility's been given in front of the weekend -- the usual gamma selling," he said, referring to the weakness in shorter-dated volatilities.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker acceleration and bigger delta swings against spot movements, but are also vulnerable to time decay.

MaryBeth Slack, FX options analyst at MCM OptionWatch, said one-week options were actually bid up when the dollar rose to a fresh six-year high of 1.8403 marks earlier in the day, marginally eclipsing Thursday's 1.8400 high.
The dollar has since rowed back slightly to hover in the mid- to upper-1.83s for most of the U.S. session, pulling down volatilities with it.
The dollar/mark volatility curve remained nearly flat, with one month trading at 10.3/10.5 percent at U.S. midsession, nearly 0.2 point off early highs.

Still, as most traders expected the dollar to eventually take out the 1.84 resistance and move higher, risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, remained skewed for mark puts. One-month 25-delta was unchanged at 0.5/0.8 percentage point in favor of mark puts.
A lot of "one-touch" options, exotic instruments incurring payoff when spot touches certain levels, have been traded with triggers at 1.98-2.00 in recent days, Slack at MCM added.
Dollar/Swiss franc volatilities rose sharply as spot extended gains to the upper-1.51-franc area after rallying on Thursday past the 1.50 level.
Slack noted that dollar/Swiss volatilities had fallen below dollar/mark volatilities earlier in the week.

"It's flip-flopped back over on realization that Swiss franc is probably not the best choice as a safe-haven currency, considering the fact that it has virtually no yield," she said. Dollar/Swiss-dollar/mark spreads returned to positive territory, at about 1.1 point in one-month and 1.5 in one-year.
Likewise, sterling/Swiss and sterling/mark spreads widened as some sizable widening plays were put on today, Slack said.
Traders said a huge amount, perhaps close to $2 billion in notional value, of short-dated 1.50 Swiss puts maturing Monday had traded in the days prior to the spot breakout.
Gamma short-covering after the rally could be one reason volatilities were so firm, noted Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York.
Dollar/yen volatilities edged up across the positively sloped curve as the dollar broke slightly above recent peaks in the upper-116-yen area.
One-month dollar/yen rose a quarter point to 9.9/10.1 percent, while one-year gained 0.2 to 10.9/11.1.
"It's a pretty mild pickup compared with what we would be seeing on a downside move in the dollar," Hiramatsu said.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
